newsitem.title: UK: Scientologists claim discrimination in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Scientologists claim discrimination in Germany.

text.p: Scientologists who said they were living in Britain because they had suffered discrimination in Germany on Wednesday handed in a message for Chancellor Helmut Kohl at the German embassy in London.
The Church of Scientology's British office said in a statement they had urged Kohl to end what it described as his government's religious intolerance towards members of the church.
The delegation said they were living in Britain because of "discrimination they experienced in Germany".

The organisation said its statement was in response to Kohl's dismissal last week of an open letter in the International Herald Tribune which accused Germany of persecuting Scientologists as Jews were treated under Hitler.
Kohl said the letter signed by 34 Hollywood celebrities including Dustin Hoffman and Goldie Hawn was "rubbish" which only showed their ignorance of Germany.

But Wednesday's statement from the Church of Scientology, the latest broadside in its bitter dispute with the German authorities, quoted delegation members as saying: "We do know what is happening in Germany as we experienced it.
"There is no doubt whatsoever that an orchestrated programme of discrimination and intolerance is being carried out."
The submission handed in at the German embassy included statements from Scientologists describing "the various forms of discrimination" they said they had experienced in Germany.
German federal and regional governments last month agreed on measures to counter what they called the Scientologists' "expansionist aims and claims to domination".
German authorities also agreed to consider putting Scientology under surveillance by the anti-extremist Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV).
The group says it has 30,000 members in Germany but the government puts the figure at between 10,000 and 20,000.
Scientology is an applied religious philosophy founded in 1954 by U.S. writer and philosopher L. Ron Hubbard. Its headquarters are in Los Angeles.
